extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short fiction or poetry to Asimov's Science Fiction magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing and submitting short science fiction, borderline fantasy/slipstream, and poetry to Asimov's Science Fiction, covering content preferences, format, submission method, rights, and payment. Intended for prospective contributors (new and established).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates and length thresholds for short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Asimov’s pays 8-10 cents per word for short stories up to 7,500 words, and 8 cents for each word over 7,500. We seldom buy stories shorter than 1,000 words or longer than 20,000 words, and we don’t serialize novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: aim for typical accepted lengths (1,000–20,000 words) and note pay structure changes at 7,500 words; novels/serials are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry payment and length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay $1 a line for poetry, which should not exceed 40 lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each poem on a separate form (see online submission guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: No reprints or simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not publish reprints, and we do not accept 'simultaneous submissions' (stories sent at the same time to a publication other than Asimov’s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit work that is unpublished and not under concurrent consideration elsewhere; violating this may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity of authorship (open to new and previously published writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asimov’s will consider material submitted by any writer, previously published or not. We’ve bought some of our best stories from people who have never sold a story before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special prior publication required — encourage first-time authors to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred story content and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, we’re looking for 'character oriented' stories, those in which the characters, rather than the science, provide the main focus for the reader’s interest. Serious, thoughtful, yet accessible fiction will constitute the majority of our purchases, but there’s always room for the humorous as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for character-driven narratives that illuminate aspects of human existence; balance seriousness with accessibility; humor is acceptable when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed and disallowed genre boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: SF dominates the fiction published in the magazine, but we also publish borderline fantasy, slipstream, and surreal fiction. No sword & Sorcery, please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit works that fit within science fiction or adjacent literary/speculative forms; avoid pure sword & sorcery fare which the magazine does not publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limits on explicit sex and violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither are we interested in explicit sex or violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid graphic sexual or violent content; focus on implied or thematically integrated material rather than explicit depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic expectation for SF submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good overview would be to consider that all fiction is written to examine or illuminate some aspect of human existence, but that in science fiction the backdrop you work against is the size of the Universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use speculative elements to explore human concerns on a broad scale; emphasize the human rather than only technological or gadget-driven plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on submissions written/assisted by AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not consider any submissions written, developed, or assisted by these tools. Attempting to submit these works may result in being banned from submitting works in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT) to write, develop, or assist submissions; full human authorship is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submissions system required (no email submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asimov’s now uses an Online Submissions System... We do not accept email submissions. Please see Manual Submission Guidelines for information about paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit electronically only via the official online portal unless following the specified manual/paper guidelines; do not send manuscripts by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission form contents and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our online submissions form for fiction asks for your name, email address, cover letter, story title, and story. Cover letter is optional. If you choose to include it, it should contain the length of your story and your publishing history. Story word count can, and should, also be indicated in the upper right corner of the first page of the manuscript. We ask for the same information for poetry. Please fill out a separate form for each poem submitted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required fields; include optional cover letter details if used; place word count on first page upper right; submit each poem separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats and manuscript formatting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories and poems should be in standard manuscript format and submitted in .DOC, .DOCX, or .RTF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 'Proper Manuscript Format' (see William Shunn’s guide). Use one of the accepted file types to avoid processing delays or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confirmation and tracking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have submitted your work, a tracking number will be displayed and an automated email confirmation containing this information will be sent to you. If you have not received this email within twenty-four hours, please notify us by email. Your tracking number will allow you to monitor the status of your submission through our website, so please don’t lose it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an automated confirmation within 24 hours; check spam folders (Yahoo.com occasionally treats our email as spam) and notify them if you do not receive confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and querying policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our average response time runs about five weeks. If you have not heard from us in 45 days, you can query us about the submission at Asimovs@mustreadbookspublishing.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait roughly five weeks before querying; send a single query after 45 days to the specified address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual (postal) manuscript format and mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to Asimov’s must be neatly typed, double-spaced on one side of the sheet only, on bond paper (no erasable paper, please). Any manuscript longer than 5 pages should be mailed to us flat. Dot matrix printouts are acceptable only if they are easily readable. Please do NOT send us submissions on disk. When using a word processor, please do not justify the right margin. If sending a printout, separate the sheets first. The manuscript should include the title, your name and address, and the number of words in your story. Enclose a cover letter if you like. All manuscripts must be accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope (if manuscript is over 5 pages, use a 9” x 12” envelope) carrying enough postage to return the manuscript. If you wish to save on postage, you may submit a clear copy of your story along with a standard (#10) envelope, also self-addressed and stamped. Mark your manuscript 'DISPOSABLE,' and you will receive our reply only. We do not suggest that you have us dispose of your original typescript. If you live overseas or in Canada, use International Reply Coupons for postage, along with a self-addressed envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed paper-submission mechanics: double-space, one-sided, include identification and word count, include appropriate SASE or clear copy + stamped envelope, mark DISPOSABLE if you do not want originals returned; do not send disks; do not justify right margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights requested upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive first English-language publication rights for one year (you may license yourself to major award anthologies without asking us). After, non-exclusive inclusion in our archive, including a place for subscribers to read your story on our websites. Non-exclusive translation rights. We are relaunching our international editions. Non-exclusive right to include your story in our anthologies. Non-exclusive paper goods rights for excerpts tied to the Magazine. Optional non-dramatic merchandise rights (if you elect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By accepting publication, authors grant Asimov’s specified exclusive and non-exclusive rights; note the one-year exclusive first-publication period and various non-exclusive downstream rights. Authors can elect optional non-dramatic merchandise rights.
